units: <cite ref="Mishnah Keritot 1:2">Ker. I, 2</cite> <he>על אלו … ועל שִׁגְגָתָם חטאת</he> for the following acts one incurs the punishment of extinction if wilfully committed, and is bound to bring a sin-offering if committed inadvertently.
<cite ref="Mishnah Keritot 2:2">Ib. II, 2</cite> <he>אלו … הזדון כש׳</he> the following must offer a sacrifice for their wilful acts as if they were inadvertent ones.
<cite ref="Shabbat 70a:1">Sabb. 70ᵃ</cite> (in Chald. dict.) <he>קרבן דחייב רחמנא אמאי אש׳</he> for what act does the Law demand a sacrifice? Only for an inadvertent act.
<cite ref="Shabbat 69a:2">Ib. 69ᵃ</cite> <he>שִׁגְגַת קרבן שמה ש׳</he> ignorance as to eventual liability to a sacrifice is called inadvertency; <cite ref="Shevuot 26b:3">Shebu. 26ᵇ</cite>.
<cite ref="Shevuot 26b:1">Ib.</cite> <he>איזוהי שגגת שבועת וכ׳</he> how is inadvertency in a vain oath with regard to a past event possible?; a. v. fr.—
<cite ref="Moed Katan 18a">M. Kat. 18ᵃ</cite>, a. fr. <he>והואי כש׳ שיוצאה מלפני השליט</he> (fr.
<cite ref="Ecclesiastes 10:5">Koh. X, 5</cite>) and it was as an error proceeding from the ruler, i.e. his ominous words, although not meant as such, came true.—Pl. <he>שְׁגָגוֹת</he>.
<cite ref="Shabbat 70a:1">Sabb. 70ᵃ</cite> (in Chald. dict.) <he>התם חדא שגגה הכא טובא ש׳ הוייו</he> there it is only one error, here there are several.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Shevuot 1:2:4">Y. Shebu. I, 33ᵃ</cite> <he>חטאתם אלו הש׳</he> ‘their sins’ (<cite ref="Leviticus 16:21">Lev. XVI, 21</cite>) this refers to inadvertent acts; a. fr.
